key_insight: A fully GPU-based pipeline combines differentiable high-fidelity simulation, neural emulation, and residual-based refinement to produce physics-consistent hypersonic flow surrogates.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, lower-cost prediction of shock-dominated flowfields for design and optimization workflows where accurate hypersonic aerodynamics are critical.
method: Use JAX-Fluids to generate training data on GPU with a differentiable high-fidelity solver.
Train neural emulators with uncertainty quantification and compare multiple architectures for scaling behavior.
Apply residual-based refinement to improve physical consistency, especially when only mesh and input parameters are available.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that residual-based refinement substantially reduces residuals, improves physical consistency, and extends reliability beyond the training distribution.
watch_item: Performance may still depend on architecture choice and the quality/coverage of the training distribution, especially for steep shock gradients and extrapolation cases.
paper_title: A fully GPU-based workflow for building physics emulators of hypersonic flows
